key_insight: The paper turns the Eshelby stability question into a quantitative geometry-vs-strain framework, linking interior strain heterogeneity to distance from ellipsoidal shape with rigorous scaling laws.
engineering_relevance: It provides practical bounds for evaluating and designing non-ellipsoidal inclusions, helping predict mechanical stability and validate finite-element models in solid mechanics.
method: Derive a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance to the ellipsoid family.
Use half-order Sobolev scaling to capture morphological length-scale effects.
Develop ellipsoidal subtraction to obtain residual-field budgets and convergent upper/lower bounds for specific inclusion shapes.
evidence_signal: The proposed bounds were tested on protruded, indented, and necked inclusions and agreed with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations.
watch_item: The framework relies on careful shape characterization and rigorous interpretation, so its practical use may be sensitive to geometry measurement error and to cases outside the stated isotropic, uniform-dilatational setting.
paper_title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
